proposedPassiveObservations.name: Shortcut receipt and routing decision
proposedPassiveObservations.minimalFutureRecord: At listener entry record monotonic sequence/time, own PID/webview/window, key/code/modifier/repeat/defaultPrevented, event target/focus role, active tab identity; record actual guard disposition: uit, no command, dialog target, visible modal, repeat, or invocation. Observe existing decisions without invoking tabToets or callbacks a second time.
proposedPassiveObservations.distinguishes: A positive entry establishes P5 listener receipt; a recorded guard explains receipt without dispatch. Accepted opslaan invocation links to observation2.
proposedPassiveObservations.cannotProve: Native CGEvent input-sent alone is not WebView delivery. Missing listener entry cannot prove OS non-delivery: earlier capture/preemption, missing observer/trace or webview/lifecycle changes remain possible. Absolute WebView non-receipt requires an independently validated earlier delivery witness; none is established here.
proposedPassiveObservations.oldGap: action011 records native postToPid/focus/dirty pre-action window, not DOM keydown entry, guard decision, handler acknowledgement or monotonic delivery timing.

Record the executed return/throw/rejection or await stage plus documentId/revision and returned DocumentOpslag result (bezig/verouderd/mislukt/afgerond and uitkomst/actueel/schoon). proposedPassiveObservations.cannotProve: Dirty title alone does not prove handler execution or matching serialiser registration. No general clean-DOCX early return exists in the reviewed path; this does not prove runtime execution.
proposedPassiveObservations.oldGap: No actual handler/gate/result trace. Pre-Q AX Save was enabled; immediately post-Q/pre-CmdS button/busy/modal/selected-document/load state was not retained. Do not infer disabled Save.

proposedPassiveObservations.name: Native payload, resolved target and actual persistence outcome
sourcePoints: src/werkbestand.ts:100-158 (schrijfTerug; prepared payload and bewaar_document invoke)
proposedPassiveObservations.minimalFutureRecord: Correlate actual final IPC body length/SHA256 (Q checked offline for this plain DOCX), token alias+own window label, actual Rust-resolved private target, typed command/result/error and executed persistence stage. Compare post-result target bytes/SHA/XML against the final IPC payload; retain source/expected target fingerprints. Distinguish tempfile creation/write_all/sync_all/persist from the final target; record errors/alternate-path outcomes if actually observed.
proposedPassiveObservations.distinguishes: Serializer Q but final IPC lacks Q points to downstream preparation before persistence. Final IPC Q plus explicit native permission/format/conflict/error status separates failed/redirected save. Different actual resolved target establishes wrong-target writing; successful target write/hash match with Q rules out missing Q at that observed persistence boundary, not later external modification.
proposedPassiveObservations.cannotProve: IPC success alone is not independent target verification. Rust can return AlleenLezen/AnderFormaat or conflict/missing outcomes, not only exceptions. A .~oos-*.tmp sibling is the intended atomic-write route, not evidence of wrong-path save. No assumption of filesystem syscall tracing or path-resolution hook availability.
proposedPassiveObservations.oldGap: No correlated IPC payload, native save return, resolved token/path, write/rename result, permissions/ACL/lock context or alternate target trace. Final unchanged file alone cannot distinguish no call, old payload, rejected write, or other target.

feasibilityAndAuthorization: These are proposed observation boundaries, NOT implemented instrumentation or claims of existing hooks. Reviewed source functions provide no complete per-attempt key/handler/payload/native-write receipt; old raw artifacts do not contain these missing signals.

Capturing any missing runtime sequence now requires a separately assigned new native session. No existing bytes can retrospectively supply it. A new run diagnoses its own observed outcome; an absent recurrence or later success cannot explain the old failure.

Before scheduling, an owner must establish feasible read-only observation for the exact signed P5 package, including code/source mapping and debugger/inspection permissions. Release WebView/native attach/logpoint availability is NOT verified or assumed. No entitlement/signature/security changes are authorized.

If available passive tooling cannot observe the boundaries, report the capability gap; an instrumented app build requires separate approval and different package identity, and cannot be claimed as the original accepted P5 signed bytes.

Future observation must not call editor getters with side effects, flush/save/setters, dispatch keys, add retries/readiness waits or alter document/focus state. Correlate existing work rather than introducing a save barrier; even passive logging/byte capture can perturb timing and must be disclosed.

Use one bounded trace attempt with monotonic identities, explicit trace-start/end/coverage and existing producer/package/PID binding. Do not infer non-delivery or non-execution from missing/unreliable logs. Parse owned synthetic DOCX payloads offline; do not collect user documents/tokens/secrets.
